dialog-title.purpose: The title of Help; 1.25rem at 520px and below. Help's section headings are 1.0625rem at 750.

card-heading.purpose: The heading of a card, and of the first run above the list.

book-title.purpose: A book in the list. Source Serif 4 is for book titles only.

book-title-details.purpose: The title at the top of Details.

body.purpose: Everything else. Running text held to 62ch to 64ch.

control.purpose: Buttons at 600; fields and selects at 400.

mark.purpose: The first line of a mark in the proof margin, in the mark's colour.

label.purpose: Table heads and filter group names. Sentence case.

small.purpose: Facts under a gauge, the legend, hints, the edition line.

code.purpose: Short technical values and tokens shown once. Tabular.

sign-in-code.purpose: The code compared by eye with Hardcover.

site-headline.purpose: The site's one h1, fluid from 2.4rem to 3.8rem, beside the download card; its own ramp, large where the page is small.

site-section.purpose: A section's h2 on the site, fluid from 1.7rem to 2.6rem; also on a card.

site-figure.purpose: A step's number on a gradient card, 6rem to 9rem at -0.06em.

site-step-figure.purpose: A step's number on a photo step card, 4.5rem to 6.5rem, so that the photograph keeps its top half.

site-line.purpose: The one paragraph on a story card, 500, held to 34ch.

site-sure.purpose: The line under Download for Mac: what it reads, what it writes, that it starts as a dry run. On Flag on the download card, white on the close's scrim.

site-lede.purpose: The line under a heading, in graphite, 60ch; white at 92% on a card.

site-body.purpose: The site's body and a step's paragraph.

site-caption.purpose: Captions, the foot, a screenshot's caption, the version line; 62ch.

site-name.purpose: The name in the head, with the Name Caret before it.

site-nav.purpose: The page's places in the head, graphite; ink and underlined on hover.

site-photo-title.purpose: A photo card's heading in the sans at 800: the park card's and It never guesses a match. Not a book title.

site-facts.purpose: The paragraph under a photo card's heading, 1rem at 94%.

site-button.purpose: Download for Mac; 1.25rem on the download card.

site-sheet.purpose: The base of the drawn row, 1.0625rem at 1.4; everything in the sheet is in em of it, so the row scales as one.

site-sheet-title.purpose: The book's title in the drawn row, Source Serif 4 at 1.0625em, 600: the Book Face Rule's one place on the site.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Light only, under the sheet and cards. none in dark, and the list's sheet dissolves below 1024px.

shadows.name: cover
shadows.purpose: A book cover lying on the sheet, in both lights.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Help and Details, over a backdrop of rgba(10, 12, 14, 0.6).

shadows.name: lightbox
shadows.purpose: A large cover, over a backdrop of rgba(10, 12, 14, 0.88).

shadows.name: nav-current
shadows.purpose: A hairline under the current page in the desk navigation.

shadows.name: site-lift
shadows.purpose: Site, light only: under the gradient and photo cards and the sheet; none at night and on the quiet cards. The cover in the sheet carries the tool's cover shadow. The app icon casts drop-shadow(0 10px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)) on the download card and drop-shadow(0 18px 30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)) on the cobalt card.

motion.name: ease-proof
motion.purpose: Expo ease-out for the strike, the write-in, the sync gauge and the disclosure chevron.

motion.name: strike
motion.purpose: The red strike draws across the old value.

motion.name: write
motion.purpose: The new value writes in from the left after its caret.

motion.name: row-stagger
motion.value: 70ms per row, up to the thirteenth row
motion.purpose: Each row's strike and write-in start 70ms after the row above.

motion.name: landed
motion.purpose: Coming back to a row after an action: a Blue Wash that fades.

motion.name: cover-in
motion.purpose: A large cover fades and grows in.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: The chevron of 'Paste a token instead' turns.

motion.name: sync-gauge
motion.purpose: While a sync runs, the red line gauge under Sync now fills by transform: scaleX(var(--p)) as the books go out; scaled, never resized.

motion.name: sync-sweep
motion.purpose: While the count is not known yet, a 30% red segment of the gauge sweeps across by translateX.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition is off; a row you came back to keeps a steady wash, and the sync gauge whose count is unknown is a faint full line (opacity 0.35).

motion.name: run-drift
motion.value: 7, 11, 17pt/s (back, middle, front), scaled with the run
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers only (the approved second authored motion): the three rows of the press run drift left; the front row moves one cover in about six seconds.

motion.name: run-stand
motion.value: exponential ease, 0.18s time constant; 3s hold after a move by hand
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers only: a row eases to a stop while a cover in it is lifted, the keyboard is in the run, or the large cover or Details is open, and eases back after.

motion.name: cover-lift
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers only: the cover under the pointer or the keyboard lifts, its shadow deepening.

motion.name: run-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers: under Reduce motion, and whenever the window is not visible, the run stands still and moves only by hand; under Reduce motion the lift does not grow and the large cover appears without moving.

motion.name: site-rise
motion.value: 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), 60ms apart by --i, from 18px below and transparent
motion.purpose: Site, once on load: the download card, the sheet and the three story cards rise into place in page order.

motion.name: site-strike-write
motion.value: strike (background-size from 0 1.5px) 0.5s at 0.9s; write-in (clip-path from the left) 0.6s at 1.1s, both cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: Site: in the sheet's row, the tool's own strike and write-in at the tool's timing, after the sheet has landed. The three story cards stand still.

motion.name: site-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Site: under prefers-reduced-motion the cards and the sheet stand in place, the strike and write-in are off, and smooth scrolling is off.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: At 520px and below: a term in Details stacks over a 6.75rem term column, Help's terms go to one column, filter group names go above their chips, Help's title is 1.25rem.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The first book and its mark on the first screen at 390 by 844: the page line and the band's 'N of M books syncing' step aside, Filter and Sort share one row.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Two book cards per row; the rail's status in three columns with the two buttons under them, to the right.

breakpoints.name: one-column
breakpoints.purpose: Rail as a top band with its own Help button (.bandhelp), bottom navigation, filters behind one button, book cards with a margin strip, the first run a card of its own, 2.75rem controls.

breakpoints.name: desk
breakpoints.purpose: The 17.25rem rail and the sheet in one window; the list scrolls in its sheet under a sticky head.

breakpoints.name: first-run-wide
breakpoints.purpose: The first run's three steps stand beside its heading and tally instead of under them.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Everything operated is 2.75rem, chips, Help and the theme switch included.

breakpoints.name: site-phone
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the story cards lose their 22rem floor (the photograph keeps 17rem, its words padded 6rem above); the four step cards go to one column and lose their 26rem floor (a photo step 16rem, its words padded 5.5rem above); the Books page's night capture and the Details capture are hidden, the phone capture is at most 14rem wide from a 400w copy, and the Mac app shows the Overview alone.

breakpoints.name: site-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the sheet's row stacks (the book, the two switches side by side with their names above them, the margin under a double rule on its top); the other tools' table stacks; the in-page links leave the head; the Mac app's icon stands above its words.

breakpoints.name: site-claim
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the claim in two columns, the headline and lede at 1.5fr beside the download card at 1fr; the story and the Mac app's pictures across; the screenshots on six columns. Below it everything is one column, the download card follows the lede, and the cards under What it does lose their 28rem floor (the photograph 18rem, its words padded 6.5rem above).

breakpoints.name: site-four
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the four step cards in one row on three shared rows (subgrid), the figures on one line; two by two below, the same.

gradients.name: plum
gradients.purpose: Site: Your computer in the story. Words at the foot, on the deep end.

gradients.name: teal
gradients.purpose: Site: Hardcover in the story. Words at the foot, on the deep end.

gradients.name: teal-list
gradients.purpose: Site: What it does; the lime is a strip at the head of the card, the heading white like every card heading, the list on the teal.

gradients.name: slate
gradients.purpose: Site: What it leaves alone, with Site Ink dark words in both lights.

gradients.name: scrim
gradients.purpose: Site: under the words at the foot of a photo card.

gradients.name: scrim-step
gradients.purpose: Site: the step cards (four slices of one photograph), the story's and the photograph under What it does, which carry a heading and a paragraph; the words are padded 11rem above (9rem on the story card) so that the top half stays photograph.

gradients.name: scrim-close
gradients.purpose: Site: the close, with the download on it; it spans the whole photograph, the words held to 46rem.

components.name: Button
components.description: The default control: sheet, Field Edge border, ink words; 2.375rem, 2.75rem below 1024px and under a finger.

components.name: Sync now, running
components.description: In the rail: Sync now names what it would send on a second line; while a sync runs it stays red but disabled and aria-busy, says Syncing and what it is doing, and a red line gauge fills by scaleX(var(--p)) or sweeps while the count is unknown; after it, one status line with its mark says what the sync did.
components.html: Done: 3 changes would be sent. This is a dry run.
components.css: .ds-rail-s{display:grid;gap:1.1rem;width:15rem;padding:1.2rem;background:var(--rail);color:var(--rail-ink);font-family:var(--sans)} .ds-sync{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:0.1rem;width:100%;min-height:2.75rem;line-height:1.2;padding:0.4rem 0.9rem;font-family:var(--sans);font-size:0.875rem;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;background:var(--red);border:1px solid var(--red);color:var(--on-fill);border-radius:var(--r-ctl)} .ds-sync small{font-size:0.75rem;font-weight:500} .ds-sync:hover{filter:brightness(1.07)} .ds-sync:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--blue);outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px} .ds-sync[aria-busy="true"],.ds-sync[aria-busy="true"]:hover{opacity:1;filter:none;cursor:progress} .ds-gauge{position:relative;height:9px;margin:0.5rem 0 0;background:repeating-linear-gradient(to right,var(--edge) 0 1px,transparent 1px 10%) left bottom/100% 4px no-repeat,linear-gradient(var(--edge),var(--edge)) left bottom/100% 1px no-repeat} .ds-gauge::after{content:"";position:absolute;right:0;bottom:0;width:1px;height:4px;background:var(--edge)} .ds-gauge span{position:absolute;left:0;bottom:1px;height:4px;width:100%;background:var(--red);transform-origin:left;transform:scaleX(var(--p,0));transition:transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)} .ds-gauge.ds-wait span{width:30%;transform:none;animation:ds-sweep 1.1s ease-in-out infinite alternate} @keyframes ds-sweep{from{transform:translateX(0)}to{transform:translateX(233%)}} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-gauge.ds-wait span{animation:none;width:100%;opacity:0.35}.ds-gauge span{transition:none}} .ds-done{font-size:0.875rem} .ds-act{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.6rem minmax(0,1fr);column-gap:0.5rem;align-items:start;color:var(--rail-ink)} .ds-act .ds-mk{width:20px;height:20px;margin-top:-0.05em} .ds-ok .ds-mk{color:var(--green)}

components.name: Solid button (ink fill)

components.name: Danger button (removing)
components.description: Removing actions: ink, no box, underlined; never red.

components.css: .ds-hc{max-width:22rem;padding:1rem 0.9rem;border-left:3px double var(--rule);background:var(--margin);font-family:var(--sans);font-size:0.875rem;color:var(--ink)} .ds-act{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.6rem minmax(0,1fr);column-gap:0.5rem;align-items:start} .ds-act .ds-mk{width:20px;height:20px;margin-top:-0.05em;color:var(--red)} .ds-act>span{font-weight:650;font-size:0.8125rem;color:var(--red)} .ds-fix,.ds-sub,.ds-details{margin-left:2.1rem} .ds-fix{margin-top:0.1rem;font-size:0.9375rem} .ds-swap{white-space:nowrap} .ds-fix s{color:var(--graphite);text-decoration:none;background:linear-gradient(var(--red),var(--red)) no-repeat 0 58%/100% 1.5px;animation:ds-strike 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) both} .ds-fix ins{display:inline-flex;align-items:baseline;gap:1px;color:var(--red);font-weight:650;text-decoration:none;animation:ds-write 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 0.2s both} .ds-fix ins svg{width:10px;height:10px;align-self:flex-end;margin-bottom:-4px} .ds-sub{color:var(--graphite);font-size:0.8125rem;margin-top:0.2rem} .ds-stet{display:inline;margin-right:0.3rem;font-style:italic;font-weight:800;font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--blue)} .ds-details{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:2rem;margin-top:0.55rem;font-size:0.8125rem;font-weight:600;color:var(--ink);text-decoration:none;background:var(--sheet);border:1px solid var(--edge);border-radius:var(--r-ctl);padding:0.15rem 0.65rem} .ds-details:hover{border-color:var(--ink)} .ds-details:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--blue);outline-offset:2px;border-radius:2px} @keyframes ds-strike{from{background-size:0 1.5px}} @keyframes ds-write{from{clip-path:inset(0 100% 0 0)}to{clip-path:inset(0 0 0 0)}} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-fix s,.ds-fix ins{animation:none}}

components.css: .ds-bk{display:grid;grid-template-columns:48px minmax(0,1fr);gap:0.95rem;align-items:start;font-family:var(--sans);color:var(--ink)} .ds-cover{display:block;width:48px;height:72px;border-radius:1px 3px 3px 1px;background-color:var(--sheet);border:1px solid var(--edge);background-image:linear-gradient(to top right,transparent calc(50% - 0.6px),var(--edge) 50%,transparent calc(50% + 0.6px)),linear-gradient(to top left,transparent calc(50% - 0.6px),var(--edge) 50%,transparent calc(50% + 0.6px))} .ds-title{font-family:var(--serif);font-size:1.0625rem;font-weight:600;line-height:1.25;letter-spacing:-0.005em} .ds-tag{display:inline-block;font-family:var(--sans);font-size:0.75rem;font-weight:700;line-height:1.1rem;color:var(--graphite);border:1px solid currentColor;border-radius:3px;padding:0 0.3rem;margin-left:0.45rem;vertical-align:0.12em} .ds-author{color:var(--graphite);font-size:0.875rem;margin-top:0.1rem} .ds-bar{position:relative;height:9px;max-width:16rem;margin:0.7rem 0 0.35rem;background:repeating-linear-gradient(to right,var(--edge) 0 1px,transparent 1px 10%) left bottom/100% 4px no-repeat,linear-gradient(var(--edge),var(--edge)) left bottom/100% 1px no-repeat} .ds-bar::after{content:"";position:absolute;right:0;bottom:0;width:1px;height:4px;background:var(--edge)} .ds-bar span{position:absolute;left:0;bottom:1px;height:4px;background:var(--ink)} .ds-meta{display:flex;gap:0.1rem 0.9rem;flex-wrap:wrap;color:var(--graphite);font-size:0.8125rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}

components.name: First-run steps
components.description: At the top of the Books sheet while in dry run: a heading, one paragraph, the ink tally of books switched on, and three numbered steps in 1.6rem circles (the one 50% radius); the current step is filled blue because it is the reader's. A double rule closes it; below 1024px it is a card of its own.
components.html:
Pick the books that are yours

Your Kobo sent 214 books. The 198 that were on it before Lastread started begin as Off, so books someone else read on a shared Kobo account stay off your Hardcover shelf. Search for an author or a title, then switch on everything shown at once.

12 switched on so far. Nothing is sent while this is a dry run.

  1. 1Connect to HardcoverNot yet. Connect in Settings

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Galley Proof"**

The list of books is a galley proof of your Hardcover shelf. Each book is a line set on the sheet, and the Hardcover column is the proof margin: what the next sync will change is marked there in proofreaders' marks, on the row itself. The old value is struck through in red, the new value is written in after a caret. A reader who looks at the page sees, per book, what Hardcover will be told and why.

The world is a print shop's, made of paper, pencil and rule. A cool grey galley stock for the page; a near-white sheet for the list; a pale non-repro blue rail that is "your Kobo" (the name, the navigation, and on Books what the Kobo and Hardcover last did, with the button that sends). Two pencils do the marking: red for what a sync sends, blue for what the reader chose or is asked. Everything else is ink and graphite. The page is dense where a proof is dense, in the list, and only the book titles are set in a book face.

It turns down the usual look for this kind of tool: a neutral list with coloured status dots and badges. A mark is drawn beside plain words, never pinned on as a badge. There are no pill shapes and no photographs; book covers are the only pictures, and the tool fetches them itself.

The site (`site/`) is a world of its own, kept apart from the tool's and the Mac app's: the claim and the download, then one row of the tool's Books page drawn at full size with the proof mark on it, on a white ground by day and a near-black one at night, and under it the three the sync runs between, the Kobo, your computer and Hardcover, one card each, with photographs of people reading as cards too. It keeps the page's two faces from its own font files, the page's marks, its one motion and its theme switch, and the drawn row keeps the tool's own colours; nothing else of the galley. Its tokens carry the `site-` prefix, the `site-sheet-` set and the three gradient families, and its rules are under *The site* in Colors and Components.
keyCharacteristics: The Hardcover column is a proof margin: a tinted column behind a double hairline rule, holding one status line per book.
Seven marks, all in the legend above the list: red caret, dashed caret, tick, *stet*, circled query, ink square with a cross, dash.
Two pencils with one job each: red for what a sync sends, blue for the reader's own choice or a question for them.
Two typefaces with one job each: Source Serif 4 for book titles, Schibsted Grotesk for everything else.
Square-cut: 2px to 4px corners, no pills; the round shapes are the ring around a Getting started step number and, in the Mac app's *Covers*, the disc under a cover's red caret.
Light and dark share every role; WCAG 2.2 AA in both.

One authored motion: the strike draws, the new value writes in. Only the Mac app's *Covers* pane has a second: the run drifts, a cover lifts. The site has one of its own, once on load: the download card, the sheet and the story cards rise into place, and the strike and the write-in follow in the sheet's row.

The site is its own world: the tool's row drawn as the hero, then the gradient cards (plum, teal, cobalt, slate) the same in both lights, 18px corners, photographs under a scrim, no rules between cards; only the download card and the sheet change with the light, the card ink by day and white at night, the sheet in the tool's two lights.

rules.name: The Two Pencils Rule
rules.body: Red fills only *Sync now* and *Go live*, and marks only what a sync sends. Every other filled button is an ink fill (*Start using Lastread*, *Connect to Hardcover*, *I have approved it*, *Use*, a confirmation, *Check and save*). Blue is only for the reader's own choice or a question for them; a label that states a fact (*New*, *Admin*) is grey. A removing action is ink, never red. The site has no red fill at all: its one filled button is the card's reverse, and the sheet carries the tool's red as a mark only.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: Every mark the margin can hold is in the legend above the list, drawn and coloured the same, with the words of the page's strings: *Next sync changes this*, *Nothing to send yet*, *Up to date*, *Kept as on Hardcover*, *Needs you*, *Failed*, *Not syncing*. Help explains each one under *Hardcover status*. A new mark is not used until it is in both.

rules.name: The Two Lights Rule
rules.body: Every colour has a light and a dark value with the same role. A colour that exists in one theme only is a mistake. In dark the red and blue are lighter and fills carry dark words (`on-fill-dark`). On the site the gradient and photo cards are the same in both lights, a card does not change with the room; the ground, the words, the quiet card, the download card and the sheet swap, the download card from ink to white and the sheet in the tool's two lights, so that the action stays the strongest thing on the ground in each light.

rules.name: The Legible Rule
rules.body: Words stand at 4.5:1 or more on whatever they are on, the edge of a field and every mark at 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA), in both themes. `tests/test_design_tokens.py` checks the pairs from `kobo.css`. The site's pairs are given under *The site* above; on a card the words stand on the dark end of the gradient, never on the bright stop.

rules.name: The Book Face Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 is for book titles and nothing else: in the list, at the top of Details, under a large cover. The name, headings, buttons and every fact are Schibsted Grotesk.

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures go only where numbers stand in columns or are compared: the facts under a gauge (`.meta`), the counts on chips, the count on the Filter button, the end of the list's count, Getting started's tally and step numbers, and code. Never on the root or on running text: in Schibsted Grotesk `tabular-nums` widens full stops and commas too. `tests/test_design_tokens.py` holds this.

rules.name: The Finger Rule
rules.body: Below 1024px fields, selects, buttons and *Details* are 2.75rem (44px), and the theme switch 2.5rem. Under a coarse pointer, at any width, everything you operate is 2.75rem, chips and the theme switch included.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are told apart by tone and a rule. A shadow is never needed to read the page; the dark theme proves it.

rules.name: The No Pills Rule
rules.body: No pill-shaped buttons, chips, tags or switches. The largest corner on anything you operate is 4px in the tool and the Mac app, and 12px on the site's one button and its theme switch, a card's rounding, still far from a pill.

dos: **Do** put what a sync will do with a book in its proof margin, as one status line with one of the seven marks.
**Do** strike the old value in red and write the new value after a red caret when the next sync changes something.
**Do** fill red only *Sync now* and *Go live*; give every other filled button the ink fill.
**Do** keep blue for the reader's own choice or a question for them.
**Do** add any new mark to the legend and to Help's *Hardcover status*, drawn and coloured the same, before it appears in a row.
**Do** set book titles in Source Serif 4 at 600 and everything else in Schibsted Grotesk.
**Do** put `tabular-nums` only on numbers that stand in columns or are compared: the facts, chip counts, the Filter count, the end of the list's count, Getting started's tally and step numbers, code.
**Do** use 2px for sheets, cards and dialogs, 4px for what you operate, and the 3px double rule where the margin begins.
**Do** make every control 2.75rem below 1024px and under a finger.
**Do** give every new colour a light and a dark value with the same role, and check it: 4.5:1 for words, 3:1 for field edges and marks.
**Do** make every action work without JavaScript, and stop every motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** draw a missing cover as the crossed box.

**Do** keep the site's cards the same in both lights, the words on the dark end of the gradient; only the download card and the sheet swap, the card ink by day and white at night, the sheet in the tool's two lights.
**Do** draw the site's marks as the page's caret, tick, circled query and dash, inline SVG: in the words' colour on a card, in the sheet's own red, green, blue and faint on the sheet.
donts: **Don't** show status as coloured dots or badges on a neutral list; the mark is drawn beside plain words.
**Don't** use red for decoration, for a warning, or for a button that removes something; a removing action is ink, underlined.
**Don't** use pill shapes, for buttons, chips, tags or switches.
**Don't** set `tabular-nums` on the root or on running text.
**Don't** set anything but a book title in Source Serif 4.
**Don't** rely on a shadow to separate surfaces; the dark theme has none.
**Don't** set labels in capitals or track them out.

**Don't** add a second authored motion; the strike and the write-in are the one. The Mac app's *Covers* pane is the one approved exception: the drift and the lift, standing still under Reduce motion and when not visible. The site's is its own one: the download card, the sheet and the story cards rise once on load and the strike and write-in follow in the sheet's row, standing still under reduced motion.

**Don't** load a font, a script, a style or a picture from elsewhere; the tool serves everything, the two fonts and the book covers included, and the site bundles its fonts and its four photographs. The site's one request out is the latest release's version, with JavaScript; without it the download link stands.
**Don't** put a kicker or an eyebrow above a heading on the site, or a hairline between its cards; colour parts them. The sheet's rules are the tool's, and stay inside the sheet.
